claim: Château de Tarascon is a 15c riverside fortress built between 1400 and 1435 by Louis II and Louis III of Anjou, counts of Provence, with 30+ rooms and a panoramic Rhône terrace; closed Mondays.
quote: The Château of Tarascon is a fortress built by the princes of Anjou on the banks of the Rhône at the start of the 15th century... Construction took place between 1400 and 1435 under Louis II and his son Louis III, dukes of Anjou, counts of Provence.

claim: Château du Roi René opens daily April–August 9am–7pm, September–March 10:30am–5pm, closed Mondays, adult admission €6.50.
quote: open every day from April 1st to August 31st from 9 A.M. to 7 P.M., and from September 1st to March 31st from 10:30 A.M. to 5 P.M., closed on Mondays, with adult admission at 6.5 Euros

claim: The Moulin de Daudet inspired Alphonse Daudet's writings (he never owned it), is a classified historic monument since 1931, and sits on a belvedere overlooking the Rhône valley.
quote: Daudet's mill, though Alphonse Daudet never owned the mill but drew inspiration from it in his writings. The Daudet mill has been classified as a historical monument since 1931

claim: Barbegal Roman flour-mill complex near Fontvieille used 16 waterwheels fed by two aqueducts and is called 'the greatest known concentration of mechanical power in the ancient world'; the site is freely accessible.
quote: a flour mill complex powered by 16 waterwheels, fed by two aqueducts bringing water to Arles, and was considered 'the greatest known concentration of mechanical power in the ancient world'

claim: Abbaye de Montmajour 2026 hours: April–May & October–March 10am–5pm, June–September 9am–6:15pm; closed Mondays in winter; adult ticket €7, last entry 1 hour before close.
quote: April 1 - May 31: 10am - 5pm; June 1 - September 30: 9am - 6:15pm; October 1 - March 31: 10am - 5pm. Closed Mondays during the October-March period. Individual admission: €7

claim: Van Gogh produced numerous drawings of Montmajour Abbey in 1888–1889, making it a notable stop on the Van Gogh route from Arles.
quote: The site particularly fascinated Van Gogh (1853-1890), who made numerous drawings there in 1888-1889.

claim: Palais des Papes in Avignon is open daily year-round; March 1–November 1 9am–7pm; visit takes ~1.5–2 hours; tickets €12 (palace), €17 with Pont d'Avignon and gardens.
quote: March 1 – November 1: 9am–7pm... Palace only: €12... Palace + Avignon Bridge + Gardens: €17... Visite du Palais des Papes : environ 1h30 – 2h

claim: Official Les Baux tourism site lists drive times of 20 km/30 min to Arles and 35 km/40 min to Avignon (so Avignon is at the practical edge of a half-day from Les Baux).
quote: Arles: 20 km (30 min); Avignon: 35 km (40 min)

claim: Abbey of Saint-Gilles is UNESCO-listed (as part of the Routes of Santiago de Compostela in France) and famed for its 1120–1160 Romanesque carved façade with three portals depicting Old/New Testament scenes.
quote: included in the UNESCO Heritage List as part of the World Heritage Sites of the Routes of Santiago de Compostela in France... The façade was built from 1120 to 1160 and features a decorated entrance portico with three portals

claim: Beaucaire Fortress is a free-to-visit 11c Counts-of-Toulouse stronghold facing Tarascon across the Rhône, with seasonal hours and rampart views; July–August daily 9:30am–8pm.
quote: The vestiges of this château médiéval can be visited free of charge all year... July 1 to August 31, 2026: Daily 09:30-20:00

claim: Saint-Rémy holds its iconic Provençal market every Wednesday morning; nearest car parks fill quickly in summer and a free shuttle runs from Petite Crau 9am–1pm every 15 minutes.
quote: The nearest parking areas are quickly full during the summer season... a free shuttle bus service from the Petite Crau car park between 9am and 1pm, running every 15 minutes.

claim: Les Baux village requires parking outside the walls; all lots are paid year-round 8am–7pm at €5 for the first hour, with no free parking and a €35 illegal-parking fine.
quote: All parking areas are paid year-round from 8am to 7pm at €5 for the first hour... There are no free parking spaces in Les Baux-de-Provence... Illegal parking is prohibited and subject to a €35 fine.

claim: In France most non-food shops close Sundays; bakeries/butchers/patisseries can open until 13:00, cafés and restaurants can open all day, and a business open Sunday often closes Monday instead.
quote: Businesses selling food such as bakeries, cheese shops, butchers, patisseries, and fishmongers are allowed to open until 13:00 on Sundays. Cafes and restaurants can open all day on Sunday... if a store or restaurant is open on Sunday, they might actually close on Monday instead.

claim: A standard 2–3 day Alpilles loop pairs Arles + Les Baux + Saint-Rémy by car since all are within easy reach, and Saint-Rémy is ~20 min from Les Baux.
quote: Arles, Les Baux de Provence and St Remy de Provence are all within easy reach of each other by car... Saint Rémy-de-Provence: 20 min, Arles: 30-40 min, Avignon: 40-50 min from Les Baux.
